# waitmatch waits for a background command to print a matching line,
# including one printed before waitmatch starts waiting,
# and sets variables to the subexpressions of the match.
! exec printandwait stdout 'starting up' 'listening on 127.0.0.1:1234' 'more output' &srv&
waitmatch srv '^listening on (.+):(\d+)$' HOST PORT
exec printargs $HOST $PORT
stdout '"127.0.0.1" "1234"'
waitmatch srv '^starting up$'
waitmatch srv '^more output$'

# Waiting for the command still gives all of its output.
kill srv
wait srv
stdout '^starting up\nlistening on 127.0.0.1:1234\nmore output\n$'

# -stderr waits for a line on standard error instead.
! exec printandwait stderr 'ready' &errsrv&
waitmatch -stderr errsrv '^ready$'

# A command may also exit before or while waitmatch waits.
exec fprintargs stdout done &short&
waitmatch short '^done$'

! testscript -v exited
stdout 'FAIL: .*: "bg" exited without printing a line matching `never` to stdout'

! testscript -timeout=500ms timeout
stdout 'FAIL: .*: test timed out while waiting for "bg" to print a line matching `never` to stdout'

! testscript usage
stdout 'unknown background process "nosuch"'
stdout 'cannot set 2 variables from 1 subexpressions'

# Lines may also end with CRLF.
[!exec:cat] stop
unix2dos crlf.txt
exec cat crlf.txt &crlf&
waitmatch crlf '^ready$'

-- exited/script.txt --
exec fprintargs stdout foo &bg&
waitmatch bg never
-- timeout/script.txt --
exec printandwait stdout foo &bg&
waitmatch bg never
-- usage/script.txt --
exec printandwait stdout foo &bg&
waitmatch nosuch foo
-- usage/twovars.txt --
exec printandwait stdout foo &bg&
waitmatch bg '(foo)' A B
-- crlf.txt --
ready
